aj: Quick sanity-check — bringing up ranker-x-small-v2 (cross-encoder) with PTQ int8 and KV-cache ON. Offline eval shows NDCG@10 down ~0.7% relative vs prod baseline on our anchor holdout. MRR also dips slightly. Anybody seen windowing/batching+KV interactions cause this? :thinking:

maria: what batch size / eval harness are you using? are you using the exact same candidate ordering + truncation as baseline?

aj: Offline run used batch=32 (cpu eval harness), baseline runs were batch=8 in prod-like bench. Command I ran:
```bash
./eval_runner --model ranker-x-small-v2-int8 --batch 32 --kv-cache on --holdout anchor_set_v4 --seed 42
```
Results summary (anchor_set_v4): baseline  NDCG@10=0.8423, MRR=0.6312
new model NDCG@10=0.8366, MRR=0.6265  (diff NDCG -0.0057 absolute)

ci-bot: Test report uploaded: https://ci/reports/2098765432/run-1. Artifacts: eval.json, logits.pkl, per-slice-ndcg.csv.

devon: two quick suspects: 1) batch size affects KV-cache eviction/sequence ordering with our streaming allocator, 2) windowing/truncation difference for long docs causing different scoring context. Try batch=8 and disable kv-cache to isolate.

aj: running those now. quick note: candidate text formatting is identical (we strip html and casefold), but there are more long-form docs in anchor_set_v4 vs baseline sample. Could be a length distribution shift.

eva: also check tokenization parity — PTQ sometimes pads/truncates differently post-quant. Compare per-doc input lengths and where the model hits max_seq. If the model is truncating the tail of passages ranking signals could be lost.

maria: +1 run with identical harness (same batch, same tokenizer binary, same truncation params). Also produce per-query diffs for top-5 to see if ties/score compression changed.

aj: uploaded new runs: batch=8 + kv-cache on -> NDCG@10=0.8398, MRR=0.6291
 and batch=8 + kv-cache off -> NDCG@10=0.8419, MRR=0.6308
Observations: disabling KV-cache nearly recovers baseline; enabling KV-cache seems to slightly compress scores under PTQ.

devon: that points at KV-cache ordering/precision interplay. Short-term plan: 1) re-run with deterministic KV eviction and compare float32 vs int8 logits for the same input; 2) add tiny calibration pass on KV accumulators or increase accumulation dtype precision if cheap.

aj: filing a quick ticket and adding smoke tests to CI harness to run int8+kv-cache with batch sizes {8,16,32} on anchor_set_v4. cc @maria @devon. Thanks all :thumbsup:
